title: UPSC CSE - Science & Tech and Basic Science - Space Science
subject: Science & Tech and Basic Science

questions.q:
With reference to radioisotope thermoelectric generators (RTGs), consider the following statements:
1. RTGs are miniature fission reactors.
2. RTGs are used for powering the onboard systems of spacecrafts.
3. RTGs can use Plutonium-238, which is a by-product of weapons development.
questions.explain: RTGs are not fission reactors but 'nuclear batteries'. They have been used in spacecraft like Voyager and Curiosity. They use Plutonium-238 for power generation.
questions.subject: Science & Tech and Basic Science

questions.q: Which one of the following statements best reflects the idea behind the Fractional Orbital Bombardment System often talked about in the media?
options: A hypersonic missile is launched into space to counter the asteroid approaching the Earth and explode it in space.
A spacecraft lands on another planet after making several orbital motions.
A missile is put into a stable orbit around the Earth and deorbits over a target on the Earth.
A spacecraft moves along a comet with the same speed and places a probe on its surface.
questions.explain: The Fractional Orbital Bombardment System (FOBS) was developed by the Soviet Union in the 1960s. The system is used to launch nuclear warheads from space. The idea behind FOBS is, a warhead is put into a stable orbit and it deorbits over the target.
questions.subject: Science & Tech and Basic Science

questions.q: The experiment will employ a trio of spacecraft flying in formation in the shape of an equilateral triangle that has sides one million kilometers long, with lasers shining between the craft. The experiment in question refers to
questions.explain: e-LISA (Evolved Laser Interferometer Space Antenna) is a plan of setting into space three spacecraft, which will fly in a triangular formation with sides one million kilometers long, trailing the earth in its orbit around the sun at a distance of over 50 million km. It has lasers shining between the craft.
questions.subject: Science & Tech and Basic Science

questions.q:
For the measurement/estimation of which of the following are satellite images and remote sensing data is used?
1. Chlorophyll content in the vegetation of a specific location.
2. Greenhouse gas emission from rice paddies of a specific location.
3. Land surface temperature of a specific location.
questions.explain: All three statements are correct. Satellite images and remote sensing data can be used to measure chlorophyll content using multispectral images, greenhouse gas emissions from rice paddies using Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data, and land surface temperature using thermal infrared remote sensing data.
questions.subject: Science & Tech and Basic Science

questions.q: Recently, scientists observed the merger of giant 'blackholes' billions of light-years away from the Earth. What is the significance of this observation?
options: Possibility of intergalactic space travel through 'wormhole' was confirmed.
questions.explain: Scientists have made detections of gravitational waves, ripples in the fabric of space and time emanating from separate black hole mergers. The US-based LIGO and Europe-based VIRGO gravitational-wave detectors have recorded gravitational waves from black hole mergers.
questions.subject: Science & Tech and Basic Science

questions.q:
In which of the following areas, can GPS technology be used?
1. Mobile phone operations
2. Banking operations
3. Controlling the power grids
questions.explain: GPS is used for mobile phone operations (e.g., cell towers use it to route phone calls), banking operations (e.g., ATMs and cash registers use it for transactions), and controlling power grids (e.g., electrical grids use it to send power to houses).
questions.subject: Science & Tech and Basic Science

questions.q:
Consider the following phenomena:
1. Light is affected by gravity.
2. The Universe is constantly expanding.
3. Matter warps its surrounding space-time.
Which of the above is/are the predictions/predictions of Albert Einstein's General Theory of Relativity, often discussed in the media?
questions.explain: All three statements are predictions of Einstein's General Theory of Relativity. Light is affected by gravity, the Universe is constantly expanding (though this was later confirmed by observations), and matter warps its surrounding space-time.
questions.subject: Science & Tech and Basic Science

questions.q:
With reference to India's satellite launch vehicles, consider the following statements:
1. PSLVs launch the satellites useful for Earth resources monitoring whereas GSLVs are designed mainly to launch communication satellites.
2. Satellites launched by PSLV appear to remain permanently fixed in the same position in the sky, as viewed from a particular location on Earth.
3. GSLV Mk III is a four-staged launch vehicle with the first and third stages using solid rocket motors; and the second and fourth stages using liquid rocket engines.
questions.explain: Statement 1 is correct. PSLVs launch satellites for Earth resources monitoring, while GSLVs are designed mainly for communication satellites. Statement 2 is incorrect as PSLV-launched satellites do not remain fixed in the sky. Statement 3 is incorrect as GSLV Mk III is a three-stage vehicle, not four-stage.
questions.subject: Science & Tech and Basic Science

questions.q:
With reference to the Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System (IRNSS), consider the following statements:
1. IRNSS has three satellites in geostationary and four satellites in geosynchronous orbits.
2. IRNSS covers the entire India and about 5500 sq. km beyond its borders.
3. India will have its own satellite navigation system with full global coverage by the middle of 2021.
questions.explain: IRNSS with an operational name of NAVIC is an independent regional navigation satellite system developed by India. Statement 1 is correct: Three satellites are in geostationary orbit and four in inclined geosynchronous orbit. Statement 2 is incorrect: It covers India and a region extending 1,500 km around it. Statement 3 is incorrect: The system was expected to be operational in early 2018 after a system check.
questions.subject: Science & Tech and Basic Science

questions.q: With reference to 'AstroSat', the astronomical observatory launched by India, which of the following statements is/are correct?\n1. Other than the USA and Russia, India is the only country to have launched a similar observatory into space.\n2. AstroSat is a 2000 kg satellite placed in an orbit at 1650 km above the surface of the Earth.
questions.explain: Statement 1 is incorrect: Other countries like the European Space Agency and Japan have also launched such observatories. Statement 2 is incorrect: ASTROSAT had a lift-off mass of about 1513 kg and was launched into a 650 km orbit.
questions.subject: Science & Tech and Basic Science

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
The Mangalyaan launched by ISRO
1. is also called the Mars Orbiter Mission
2. made India the second country to have a spacecraft orbit the Mars after USA
3. made India the only country to be successful in making its spacecraft orbit the Mars in its very first attempt
questions.explain: Statement 1 is correct: Mangalyaan is also known as the Mars Orbiter Mission (MOM). Statement 2 is incorrect: India was the fourth country after Roscosmos, NASA, and the European Space Agency to reach Mars orbit. Statement 3 is correct: India is the first nation in the world to reach Mars orbit in its first attempt.
questions.subject: Science & Tech and Basic Science

questions.q:
In which of the following activities are Indian Remote Sensing (IRS) satellites used?
1. Assessment of crop productivity
2. Locating groundwater resources
3. Mineral exploration
4. Telecommunications
5. Traffic studies
questions.explain: IRS satellites are used for assessment of crop productivity, locating groundwater resources, and mineral exploration. They are not used for telecommunications (INSAT satellites are used for this) or traffic studies.
questions.subject: Science & Tech and Basic Science

questions.q: The term 'Goldilocks Zone' is often seen in the news in the context of
options: the limits of habitable zone above the surface of the Earth
regions inside the Earth-like planets in outer space
search for the Earth-like planets in outer space
search for meteorites containing precious metals
questions.explain: The Goldilocks zone refers to the habitable zone around a star where it is not too hot and not too cold for liquid water to exist on the surface of surrounding planets. It is used in the context of searching for Earth-like planets in outer space.
questions.subject: Science & Tech and Basic Science

questions.q:
In the context of modern scientific research, consider the following statements about 'IceCube', a particle detector located at South Pole, which was recently in the news:
1. It is the world's largest neutrino detector, encompassing a cubic kilometre of ice.
2. It is a powerful telescope to search for dark matter.
3. It is buried deep in the ice.
questions.explain: All statements are correct. IceCube is the world's largest neutrino detector, it can be used to search for dark matter, and it is buried deep in the Antarctic ice.
questions.subject: Science & Tech and Basic Science

questions.q:
Which of the following pairs is/are correctly matched?
Spacecraft - Purpose
1. Cassini-Huygens - Orbiting the Venus and transmitting data to the Earth
2. Messenger - Mapping and investigating the Mercury
3. Voyager 1 and 2 - Exploring the outer solar system
questions.explain: Pair 1 is incorrect: Cassini-Huygens was a mission to Saturn, not Venus. Pairs 2 and 3 are correct: Messenger was for Mercury, and Voyager 1 and 2 explore the outer solar system.
questions.subject: Science & Tech and Basic Science

questions.q:
A team of scientists at Brookhaven National Laboratory including those from India created the heaviest antimatter (anti-helium nucleus). What is/are the implication/ implications of the creation of antimatter?
1. It will make mineral prospecting and oil exploration easier and cheaper.
2. It will help probe the possibility of the existence of stars and galaxies made of antimatter.
3. It will help understand the evolution of the universe.
questions.explain: Statement 1 is incorrect: Antimatter creation does not directly affect mineral or oil exploration. Statements 2 and 3 are correct: It can help in probing the existence of antimatter in the universe and understanding its evolution.
questions.subject: Science & Tech and Basic Science

questions.q:
Which of the following is/are cited by the scientists as evidence/evidences for the continued expansion of the universe?
1. Detection of microwaves in space
2. Observation of redshift phenomenon in space
3. Movement of asteroids in space
4. Occurrence of supernova explosions in space
options: None of the above can be cited as evidence
questions.explain: Scientists use the detection of cosmic microwave background radiation (1) and the observation of redshift in light from distant galaxies (2) as evidence for the continued expansion of the universe.
questions.subject: Science & Tech and Basic Science

questions.q:
Satellites used for telecommunication relay are kept in a geostationary orbit. A satellite is said to be in such as orbit when:
1. The orbit is geosynchronous.
2. The orbit is circular.
3. The orbit lies in the plane of the earth's equator.
4. The orbit is at an altitude of 22,236 km.
questions.explain: A geostationary orbit is geosynchronous (1), circular (2), and lies in the plane of the Earth's equator (3). However, the altitude is approximately 35,786 km, not 22,236 km (4 is incorrect).
questions.subject: Science & Tech and Basic Science
